More sales. Less profit. How does that happen?

Revenue growth can look encouraging while gross margins tell a different story. Product mix, discounts, and selling prices can all influence how much profit those sales generate.

My Workforce Performance & Sales Activity Power BI Kit includes product and location analysis alongside revenue and profitability measures: https://garrettsdevdesk.etsy.com/listing/4595444828/power-bi-sales-performance-dashboard

Two products can generate similar revenue and contribute very different amounts of gross profit.

Looking at sales totals alone may cause you to overlook which products are actually supporting profitability. Comparing revenue and gross profit side by side adds useful context.

Try reviewing your five highest-revenue products and ranking them again by gross profit. Do the rankings change? If so, what might explain the differences?

A change in product mix can affect profitability even when total sales are growing.

Units sold, average selling prices, discounts, and gross margins help explain what customers are buying and how those purchases contribute to results. Each measure adds another piece of the picture.

My Workforce Performance & Sales Activity Power BI Kit includes editable product performance reporting: https://garrettsdevdesk.etsy.com/listing/4595444828/power-bi-sales-performance-dashboard

The location with the highest sales isn't automatically the most profitable.

Different product mixes, selling prices, and gross margins can produce very different results across locations. Understanding those differences helps you evaluate performance with more context.

Try comparing your locations by revenue, gross profit, and gross margin percentage. Which location changes position when you move from sales rankings to profitability rankings?

Sales growth deserves a closer look before you decide how well the business is performing.

Product profitability, location comparisons, and gross margins can reveal details that a revenue trend alone won't show. Bringing these measures together helps support more informed reviews.

Revenue growth can be exciting, but it doesn't always translate into stronger profitability.

Changes in product mix, discounts, selling prices, and location performance can affect how much gross profit a business generates. That's why it helps to examine the drivers behind the headline numbers.

For analysts and business owners, what's the first metric you check when revenue is increasing but profitability isn't keeping pace?
